_comment: Expected verdicts for the design-drift fixture (cmd/browser-agent/internal/testpages/pages/design-drift.html). ONE source of truth: the Go analyzer tests and UAT category 36 both assert against this file. Three hand-maintained lists would drift apart, and the negative controls are the half that actually constrains precision, so they are listed here as explicit zero-finding expectations rather than left implicit. Every case also declares expect_elements and a confidence for each finding, so a case cannot pass on a blank or malformed response: an empty payload fails the element-count and envelope assertions before the (vacuously equal) empty finding lists are ever compared.

cases.name: step_cards_font_drift
cases.why: Step 2's header renders Roboto 11px while Steps 1 and 3 render Inter 12px. The majority is 2 of 3, which is a real majority but not a strong one, so confidence is low.

cases.name: token_cards_near_miss
cases.why: padding:15px near-misses --spacing-md:16px on all four longhands, and #2b56e2 near-misses --color-primary-main:#2a55e1. The page declared those tokens; it never declared that THIS element's padding must use them, so the last step is the analyzer's proximity inference and the finding is inferred/warning. Only a caller-supplied spec states a rule the element can break. The four longhands carry one identical verdict and the author wrote one declaration, so they collapse to a single `padding` finding — reporting the same edit four times is what multiplied 40 identical cards into 200 findings and pushed the response past the 100KB clamp. Element 1 is the exact-match control and must contribute nothing.

cases.name: rhythm_gap_drift
cases.why: Gaps run 24/24/14/24 down the stack. The modal gap is 24 (3 of 4), so the 14px gap before element 3 is the outlier. Reported against the element that follows the bad gap, which is the one whose margin produced it. Confidence is low, not high: 3 of 4 is 0.75, under the 0.8 strong-majority bar, and a four-gap stack genuinely is weaker evidence than a ten-gap one.

cases.name: spec_overrides_inference
cases.why: With a declared spacing scale that omits 24 and 14, every gap violates a stated rule. This is the case inference alone cannot catch: the page is uniformly wrong, so the majority IS the wrong value. Severity flips to error because a declared rule was broken, and confidence is high on every one: the caller stated the scale, so grading the verdict by how many gaps share a modal value would report the page's uniformity as doubt about the caller's own rule.

cases.name: default_all_categories_reconciles_contradictions
cases.why: The DEFAULT call — no `categories`, all three analyzers — on the stack whose gaps run 24/24/14/24. Every other case narrows categories, which is why this shipped: design_tokens saw margin-top:14px as a near-miss of --spacing-md (16px) at confidence:high while spacing measured the same 14px against the 24px rhythm at confidence:low, so an agent triaging by confidence applied 16px and made the page worse. Only the measured gap survives; the rejected proximity guess is folded into its evidence rather than dropped. design_tokens and style_consistency complete with nothing, which is the point — a category that ran and found nothing is not a skip.

cases.name: declared_font_spec_on_a_pair
cases.why: The same two-element group as two_element_group_control, but with the font stated. A declared rule needs no majority: element 1 renders Roboto against a spec naming Inter, which is a violation, not a coin flip. Checking peer count before consulting the spec made a rule the caller explicitly supplied unenforceable on every group of two — the one case where inference has nothing to offer either.

cases.name: declared_scale_on_a_pair
cases.why: One gap is its own norm under inference, but a declared scale states which gaps are legal, so the single 12px gap between the two pair items is judgeable on its own. Without this, a stated spacing rule was unenforceable on any pair.

cases.name: state_variant_control
cases.why: The active item is bold and blue on purpose. State is not drift, so it is excluded from the peer group rather than reported at low confidence — a finding about it would be noise however it is labelled, and leaving it in would also skew the majority the other items are judged against.

cases.name: first_child_margin_control
cases.why: The first card carries a 48px top margin where its siblings carry 24px. Structural position is not drift, and a first child's own top margin creates no gap between siblings, so the measured rhythm stays uniform.

cases.name: flex_gap_control
cases.why: Spacing here belongs to the parent's gap property, not to any child margin. The gaps are uniform so nothing is reported; the attribution path itself is covered by the Go table test, which asserts the message names the parent.

cases.name: two_element_group_control
cases.why: Two elements with different fonts have no majority — each value is as likely to be the correct one. Reporting insufficient_peers is the honest answer; picking one would be a coin flip presented as a verdict.

cases.name: out_of_flow_control
cases.why: The third card is position:absolute, so it takes no part in the rhythm. Counted, the run reads 10px, an 18px overlap, 24px and 24px, and the group reports a layout break nobody can see. This is the only fixture group carrying an in_flow:false element, so it is what proves the wire field survives translation into the analyzers instead of being read as true.
